Any attempt to involve Jamaican government against its will at this time would result in net loss of cooperation now and in future. Station regards increasing cooperation of RUABBE service in Cuban objectives of considerable value. COS believes it advantageous to KUBARK and ODYOKE for AMBUD stay out of Jamaica until sentiment changes.

title: KNGS 0202: Cuban Problem Coverage from Jamaica
summary: This cable discusses the possibility of extending coverage of the Cuban problem from Jamaica, but believes a delegation such as AMBUD whose presence overt would prove counterproductive. It also discusses the progress made in gaining covert support through RUABBE for CI effort against Cubans and requests HQS consider assignments proposed by COS.

title: Meeting with Dr. MIRO Cardona on 6 October
summary: Memorandum for the record regarding a meeting with Dr. MIRO Cardona on 6 October 1961. Topics discussed include propaganda efforts, underground activities, commando action plans, requests for arms, information on arms received by the Castro regime, a proposal for the Council to establish a government on Cuban soil, views on judges and lawyers, members of the Revolutionary Council, the probable Argentine rupture of relations with Cuba, MIRO's attendance at a homage for LACERDA, organization of the Propaganda Commission, MIRO's views on potential leaders of a provisional government, offices of the Council, coordination of exile group activities, and a telephone conversation with MIRO.

title: Reports and Information on Hada Rosete
summary: This document contains various reports and information regarding Hada Rosete, including her background, activities, and affiliations. Mentions her work in media, involvement with the Revolutionary Council, and contact information.

title: Recontact of Oliverio A. TOKKU Pasallo
summary: Recontact of Oliverio A. TOMEU Vasallo, providing additional detail on Carlos and Ana Gloria de VARONA, and identified Owiel GONZALEZ and one 'COCO' as possible leads to Jose LLANGRA Gobel.

title: REQUEST FOR APPROVAL OR INVESTIGATIVE ACTION - Santiago ALTATA Fernandez - PROJECT: JYATE
origin_agency: CI/Operational Approval and Support Division, Security Support Division/Office of Security
recipient: CI/Operational Approval and Support Division, Security Support Division/Office of Security
summary: Request for provisional operational approval for Santiago ALTATA Fernandez, associated with PROJECT: JYATE, for use in Cuba as FW Trainee. Includes security checks and limitations.

title: Report on P.H. KOETRLOCK and Individual Named CHARLES
summary: This document details information regarding P.H. KOETRLOCK's interactions with an individual named CHARLES who expressed concerning opinions about President Kennedy. It also covers KOETRLOCK's other activities and contacts.

title: Radio New York Worldwide - WRUL Broadcast Agreement and Invoices
sender: Richard W. Grefe, Vice President, Radio New York Worldwide
summary: This document contains invoices, broadcast agreements, and disbursement vouchers related to Radio New York Worldwide and Dade County Medical Society's Spanish service programs on WRUL.

title: Radio Program "El Medico y Usted" Listings
summary: Listings of radio programs titled "El Medico y Usted" (The Doctor and You) broadcasted in Cuba during the 1960s. The programs cover a range of medical topics.

title: Cable regarding QHOP/1's return to Havana
summary: This cable discusses a letter received in New York stating that QHOP/1 is due to return to Havana on April 6 to have a good position in the office of Vice Minister Arnold Rodriguez.

title: Cable Regarding Cuba and Related Matters
summary: This cable discusses Delorry's arrival in Italy, a dinner party for him by Fidel Castro in Cuba, Annie de Quendoz's relationships, letters for Luis Amado-Blanco, Roselio Montegro Quasp, Manuel Perez Hernandez, Ricardo Subirana y Lobo, Saverio Tutino, Protestant clerics in Cuba, Gustavo Arcos y Banatics in Belgium, and an index cand.

title: Meeting with AMLASH-1 in Paris, 31 January to 3 February 1965
summary: Memorandum detailing a meeting with AMLASH-1 in Paris from January 31 to February 3, 1965, discussing security implications related to Modesto Orlando Orozco Basulto's infiltration into Cuba, updates on AMLASH-1's activities, and information gathering on Cuban officials and political developments.

title: SUBJECT: Federico PALMIERI Guillermo
summary: This memo concerns Federico PALMIERI Guillermo, a former CIA agent, who is writing a book titled "My Seven Years with CIA." The memo details his current employment in El Salvador, his potential publisher in Mexico City, and his previous work with Roger RUSS. Copies of the memo are being placed in the files of individuals known to be affiliated with the Agency.

title: REQUEST FOR PCS OVERSEAS EVALUATION
summary: Request for PCS Overseas Evaluation for Calvin W. Hicks to be an OPS Officer in La Paz, Bolivia.

title: HIDALGO, Balmes, Jr.
summary: This memo concerns Balmes HIDALGO, Jr., a covert employee of the Agency in the United States for training, and the Immigration and Naturalization Service's (INS) interest in contacting him regarding Communist activities. It discusses coordinating any INS contact with Staff C/ICB and WH, due to the sensitivity of HIDALGO's potential assignments, and suggests that INS submit questions through the Agency to avoid jeopardizing his future use. The memo also addresses a security breach by HIDALGO's father, who disclosed his Agency employment to an INS inspector.

title: HIDALGO, Jr., Balmes Nieves
summary: This memo discusses the availability of Balmes Nieves Hidalgo, Jr. for testimony or interviews regarding subversive activities. It details CIA's involvement in potentially facilitating questions and answers between the FBI and Hidalgo, who is a contract employee in Panama under the Travel Control Project.

title: HIDALGO, BALMES N., JR. - OVERT AND COVERT
summary: This document details information about Balmes N. Hidalgo Jr., a GS-11 employee in the WH division, including his past work with the FBI, his operational and security clearances, and information about his parents' security clearances.

title: MOVIMIENTO DEMOCRATICA CRISTIANO
summary: Memorandum regarding MOVIMIENTO DEMOCRATICA CRISTIANO and its correspondence with Hungarian Freedom Fighters Inc.

title: SWENSON, Harold F.
sender: Laurence G. Parr, Chief, Employee Activity Branch
summary: This document pertains to the review of Harold F. Swenson's file in connection with the presentation of a Retirement Medallion and a request for cover considerations.

title: DYVOUR/ADMIN/PERSONNEL James B. Wilcott Jr. Debriefing of - Resignation in field
summary: This document details the debriefing and resignation of James B. Wilcott Jr. from KUBARK, including his employment history and instructions for future employment inquiries.

title: Full Clearance Requests on WH/C/JMWAVE Staff Agents Converting to Staff Employee Status
sender: Chief, Contract Personnel Division/Office of Personr
summary: This memorandum requests full security clearances for staff agents converting to staff employee status within WH/C/JMWAVE.

title: VITATE, Guy, Establishment of Official Cover Backstop
sender: JOSEPH M. ADAMS, Chief, Official Cover & Liaison, CCD
summary: This memo discusses the establishment of official cover backstopping for Guy Vitate, utilizing the U.S. Army Element, Joint Operations Group. It outlines procedures for managing his Unit ID card and coordinating changes in his headquarters status with the Official Cover and Liaison Section, CCD.

title: Transmittal of Blank Documentatia
summary: This dispatch transmits blank documents, including a City of Newark, New Jersey Birth Certificate, a New York driver's license instruction sheet, a National Geographic Travel-Lite Series blank Identity Card, a Flamingo Hotel identity Card, a blank Social Security card, a cachet of the Department of Labor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico with ink pad and assorted cellophane sheets used for lamination.

title: Traces on Alberto Lleras Camargo and the Hudson Institute
summary: This memo discusses Alberto Lleras Camargo and the Hudson Institute, including Lleras's background, political career, and relationship with the United States. It also mentions derogatory information on several members of the Hudson Institute and seeks guidance on future association with AMRASZ/1.

title: Project WUBRINY - Luis Albert Ferre and Antilles Materials Company Limited (AMCO)
summary: This collection of documents pertains to the Agency's interest in Luis Albert Ferre and Antonio Luis Ferre, including security approvals and discussions related to Project WUBRINY and Antilles Materials Company Limited (AMCO). It covers meetings with SKEWER/1, assessments of AMCO's commercial viability, and potential collaboration with the Puerto Rican Cement Company.

title: Operational/REDWOOD/LCIMPROVE/AELADLE ACTION REQUIRED - Michael WYNNE-ELLIS
summary: This document is a dispatch from the Chief of Station, London, to the Chief, WE, regarding Operational/REDWOOD/LCIMPROVE/AELADLE ACTION REQUIRED concerning Michael WYNNE-ELLIS and includes comments and questions about a KGB document.

title: Highlights of Tape-Recorded Conversation in Hand Between Mr. William D. Pawley and an Unidentified Cuban during Period 17-18 October
summary: Memorandum regarding a tape-recorded conversation between William D. Pawley and an unidentified Cuban about plans for sabotage against Castro and the need for moral and financial support from the U.S.

title: GENERAL- Operational SPECIFIC- PAWLEY Business Interests in the Dominican Republic
summary: Dispatch regarding William D. PAWLEY's business interests in the Dominican Republic, including mineral exploitation, purchase of Hotel Hamaca, and concession for Dominican postage stamps managed by Edward F. PALLEY.

title: LIRING-3
summary: This document appears to be a technical interrogation report from the Office of Security. It is marked as 'GROUP 1'. It also mentions the House Select Committee on Assassinations.

title: Request for Training for Six-Man Leader Group
summary: This document details a request for training for a six-man leader group scheduled to arrive at SOLATIO on July 11. It includes details on their previous training, specific skills requested for training, and logistical support for transportation.

title: JMZIP - Cuban Vice Minister's Travel Plans
summary: This cable discusses Cuban Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Carlos Olivares's plans to travel to Brazil via Mexico to promote the Cuban Revolution. It requests information on Olivares and his travel plans.

title: MEMORANDUM FOR THE RECORD SUBJECT: Meeting with AMBANG-1
summary: Memorandum for the Record regarding a meeting with AMBANG-1 on July 27, 1963 in Miami. Topics discussed include requests for high explosives, contact in Guantanamo, political plans, isolation of Cuba, phasing out of employment, a JURE radio link, aerial maps of Cuba, JURE organization and strength, ARTIME activities in Central America, a list of Cuban diplomats, relation with Jorge Volsky, two man underwater craft, training in simple scorch system, and an article for Cuadernos.

title: Information on Individuals in Mexico City
summary: This document contains information on FERNANDO PALKUZUKIA, MARIA FRANCISCA CRESPO FALCON, and HOWARD ANDERSON in Mexico City. It includes personal details such as date and place of birth, physical descriptions, passport numbers, and addresses. The document also lists various codes and initials such as RIDAT TIPIC, DIR 86283, SAS/SEC: MKH or G, ΙΛΙ/3/ΜΕΧΙ, C/WH/3, C/WMD, and references to EASING OFFICER, SACREA, and DESMOND FITZGERALD.

title: 230 VA STING WRTELLETTER EVODYING FOLLOWING IDEAS
classification: John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Act of 1992
summary: This document is a letter discussing potential business dealings involving the purchase and delivery of unspecified articles. The author expresses concerns about payment delays and requests a response to the letter. The document also includes instructions for sending a reply to a specific address.

title: Classified Message Regarding Mexico City, Bogota, Lena, and Guatemala
summary: This document is a classified message sent from the Director to Mexico City, Bogota, Lena and Guatemala. It references CA, CA/PEG, CA, PROP, WH 7 and VR. Mentions Grace Holmes and P.O. Box 1767, Coral Gables, Florida.

title: RELEASE UNDER THE PRESIDENT JOHN F. KENNEDY ASSASSINATION RECORDS ACT OF 1992
summary: This document appears to be related to the release of information under the John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Act of 1992. It includes alphanumeric codes, geographic locations, and potentially names or organizations. Further analysis is needed to determine the specific content.

title: FORTY-SIXTH ANNIVERSARY OF FOUNDING OF SOVIET STATE SECURITY ORGANIZATION
summary: This cable discusses the anniversary of the founding of the Soviet State Security Organization and suggests discreet gatherings in embassies or other locations. It also mentions previous tentative identifications and ADAMAKES MOUNT UNILATERAL UNVEILLANCE.

title: Report on Arms Cache and Motor Shipments
summary: This document discusses the ordering and shipment of arms and motors, potential caches, and related investigations.

title: CARA HARA NAVE DODS 69778 MAKI LIMA PACY GUAT
summary: This cable discusses surfacing evidence of Castro financing terrorist and pro-Cuban acts.

title: World Briefs
summary: This cable contains world briefs covering various geopolitical situations, including Berlin talks, Yugoslavian leadership, North Vietnam propaganda, Cuban involvement with the Soviet Union, Soviet economic plans, Italian government stability, Cuban-African relations, British foreign policy, British Guiana politics, French-Chinese trade, Finnish cabinet crisis, South Korean politics, Turkish cabinet crisis, Congolese political instability, and Laotian political and military dynamics.

title: Coded Message Regarding Operations and Personnel
summary: This document appears to be a coded cable message discussing operations, personnel, and traffic handling. It references individuals or entities such as MEIRV BOW, HAFELE ODXOKE, and mentions traffic being handled by OTTAWA. The document emphasizes secrecy and restrictions on reproduction.

title: REQUEST TRAINED HERBERT YAMADA
summary: This cable discusses Herbert Yamada, including his history and travels, and states there is no objection to him with liaison checks providing no operational interest shown.

title: Possible Defection of Cuban Delegation Member
summary: Cable discusses a possible defection of Antonio De Souza Carbajal, a member of the Cuban delegation, after contact with LITAMIL-3 in New York. Request for traces, comments, and advice on another trip by L-3 to New York for the purpose of talking to De Souza.

title: REQUEST TRACES AND POA BENITO RUIZ SUAREZ
recipient: DOP, ADDP, C/CI, C/SAS 5, FF VR
summary: This cable discusses Benito Ruiz Suarez, his background, connections, and travel habits. It requests traces and POA on him, noting his DOB, wife's name, and former role as a manager at the Hotel Nacional in Havana. He is identified as a former agent and sole Cuban delegate to the ACTA convention.

title: MEXI 5620: JORGE ANTONIO ABASOLO GARCIA - Traces and POA Request
summary: Cable from Mexico City requesting traces and POA for Jorge Antonio Abasolo Garcia, a Cuban industrial engineer with connections to Ernesto "Che" Guevara, and reporting on his brother Gustavo Abasolo, who is anti-Castro and potentially willing to provide information. The cable also mentions Abasolo's planned departure from Cuba and his ex-wife's family connections.

title: Robert P. Wheeler Personnel Records
sender: F. W. M. Janney, Director of Personnel; W. E. Colby, Director; R. L. Austin, Jr., Recorder
summary: This document contains personnel records and correspondence related to Robert P. Wheeler's retirement from the CIA, including his Distinguished Intelligence Medal and letters of appreciation.

title: WIROGUE Contract and Termination Documents
sender: Contract Approving Officer, Africa Division, SR/DOB
recipient: Chief, Finance Division; Contract Personnel Division; Special Contracting Officer
summary: This file contains documents related to the engagement and termination of Ernest G. Maycrink (WIROGUE/1) as an independent contractor for the CIA, including contracts, financial transactions, and agreements regarding compensation, benefits, and secrecy.

title: Personnel Actions for James S. Woods
summary: This document contains various personnel action forms and memoranda related to James S. Woods, including requests for reassignment, promotion, voluntary retirement, and commendation for exceptional performance. It covers actions from 1976 to 1978.

title: PERMINDEX CORP. ICD DOCUMENTS
summary: This file contains memos regarding the Permindex Corporation and the World Trade Center, including requests for information and background checks. It mentions Ferenc Nagy, Enrico Mandel-Mantello and other individuals associated with Permindex.

title: Summary of S/W Training and Issuance of Materials for AGENT AMLASH/1
summary: This memorandum details the S/W (secret writing) training provided to agent AMLASH/1 in Paris during August 1962, including instruction on techniques, materials, and communication protocols. It also outlines the supplies issued to the agent and specific procedures for maintaining secure correspondence.

title: GENERAL - Administrative SPECIFIC - Arthur G. VAIVADA
summary: This dispatch discusses Arthur G. VAIVADA's agreement to conversion to the career agent category and his request for his wife's U.S. citizenship to be processed for security reasons.

title: Cuban Revolutionary Council - Internal Security - Cuba
summary: This memorandum discusses the Cuban Revolutionary Council's reaction to the United States' policy towards Cuba in April 1963, including Dr. Jose Miro Cardona's potential resignation and the Council's concerns about peaceful co-existence with Communist Cuba.

title: IN 41885: MIAMI HERALD ARTICLE ON MIRO AND MANUEL RAY
summary: This cable discusses a Miami Herald article by James Buchanan which alleges Manuel Ray has replaced Miro as the leader of Cuban exiles with the backing of several Latin American leaders and the United States. The article is causing concern among Cuban exiles, and the cable suggests the need to discredit Buchanan's story and reassure Miro.

title: THE LEE HARVEY OSWALD CASE #351164
summary: This memo discusses Abram Chayes and Samuel Wise's involvement in Lee Harvey Oswald's case and their potential connections to communism.

title: Description of JMWAVE Components
summary: This document describes the organization and components of JMWAVE, including its Support Branch, Operations Branch, Covert Action Branch, External Operations Branch, Reports Section, Technical Services Section, and Communicators. It also includes organizational charts for JMWAVE and the Deputy Director for Plans.

title: Mexico City Station Operations Report
summary: This document provides an overview of the Mexico City Station's operations, including Cuban, Soviet, and other activities. It discusses personnel, resources, and recommendations for improving effectiveness.

title: Daily Summary - 6 December 1963
summary: Daily summary of intelligence related to Cuba, including military developments, international relations, internal situation, economic development, insurgency, foreign service, air flight connections, shipping support, relations with China and other blocs, and support of external subversive activities.

title: Weekly Review - Office of Current Intelligence - 27 December 1963
summary: This document is a weekly intelligence review from the Central Intelligence Agency, dated December 27, 1963. It covers various global events and situations, including Soviet trade activity, Chinese Communist leaders' tour in Africa, East German reactions to Berlin travel relaxation, North Korea's improved air defense, South Vietnam's political situation, and other international issues.

title: Kent Extract
summary: This document is an extract detailing the career of Mr. William M. Kent, who joined the Agency in December 1951 and retired after 26 years of service. It highlights his assignments, performance, and commendations, including his work during the 'Chilean crisis.' The document recommends that he be awarded the Career Intelligence Medal.

title: Annual Fitness Report - George Joannides
summary: This document contains multiple fitness reports and a memorandum in lieu of a fitness report for George Joannides, an Operations Officer. The reports cover periods from 1962 to 1979, evaluating his performance in various roles, including as Deputy Chief of Branch and involvement in covert action operations.

title: NOTES FOR MR. McCONE
summary: This memo contains notes for Mr. McCone from October 1, 1963, covering topics such as General Chiang Ching-kuo's visit to the U.S., a proposal to send Dr. Cavanagh to Rome, an assessment of the reliability of Penkovskiy's documentary material, a briefing on the program against Cuba, congressional debates on the test ban treaty, a recommendation on the Agency's standing in Congress, efforts to obtain a replacement for Colonel Grogan, a briefing on the Agency's covert action programs, a meeting about personnel security, and a letter confirming Frank Hand's assignment.

title: Memoranda regarding Covert Activities Against Cuba and Vietnam
summary: Minutes from 303 Committee meeting on June 18, 1964, discussing autonomous operations, Artime's operations, Cuban exiles' assassination plans, and psyops leaflets. Also includes minutes from Special Group Meeting (5412) on April 2, 1964, discussing North Vietnam operations, SWIFT and NASTY craft, reconnaissance, U-2 overflights, infiltration/exfiltration in Cuba, political action in Chile and Zanzibar. Also includes minutes from a Meeting of 5412 Group on February 27, 1964, discussing SAC planes operations in South Vietnam, infiltration/exfiltration of Cuba, NRO activities, and political action in Kenya. Additionally includes a memorandum from February 10, 1964, regarding clandestine and covert activities against Cuba.

title: Memorandum for the Record - DCI Meetings
summary: Memorandum for the record detailing DCI meetings and subjects covered from April to July.

title: March 1963 Memoranda Regarding Cuba, Soviet Plans, and Unauthorized Raids
recipient: All Members of the RIC Executive Committee
summary: This collection of memoranda and notes from March 1963 discusses US policy towards Cuba, including potential responses to Soviet actions, dealing with Cuban exile groups, and concerns about unauthorized raids. It also covers discussions on multilateral forces and concerns about European contributions to NATO.

title: Meetings with President Johnson on Cuba, Vietnam, and Other Matters
sender: Marshall S. Carter/Desmond FitzGerald/ McCone/ JAM/тс/mc/mcm/mfb/WE/Naud by DDCD/ Naud by DDCD/Σ/г/тс/ Jam:
summary: Memoranda record meetings with President Johnson in December 1963 regarding Cuba, Vietnam, Soviet relations, and personnel changes.

title: Memoranda regarding Cuba and Vietnam activities
summary: This collection of memoranda primarily concerns CIA activities related to Cuba, including efforts to prevent provocative actions against Cuba, negotiations for the release of Cuban prisoners, and an analysis of Castro's potential impact in the Western Hemisphere. It also includes memoranda regarding CIA activities in South Vietnam and communication channels to various communist entities.

title: Daily Planner Entries, 1959-1960
summary: This document contains entries from a daily planner, including appointments, meetings, and social engagements. The entries span from 1959 to 1960 and include names of individuals and organizations.

title: Operational Plan for Continuing Operations Against Cuba
summary: This memorandum outlines an operational plan for CIA actions against Cuba for the predictable future, focusing on intelligence efforts and long-term operations. It assumes no US invasion or support for a revolt, limited paramilitary actions, and a continued Castro regime. The plan aims to isolate and discredit the regime, maintain economic and political pressures, and gather intelligence. It includes espionage, sabotage, and psychological warfare strategies, along with recommendations for organizational changes and actions.

title: Operational/GYROSE Operational Debriefings
summary: This dispatch from the Chief of Station, JMWAVE, details operational debriefings of individuals processing through the CAC in May 1962. Subjects include former professionals, members of resistance groups, and individuals with potential connections to intelligence or counter-revolutionary activities. The debriefings covered topics like intelligence on Cuban infrastructure, potential recruitment, and leads for further operational exploitation.

title: AMCANOE
summary: This memorandum concerns U.S. contacts for a resistance group in Cuba, specifically the Unidad de Liberacion Nacional (ULN), and their plans to overthrow Castro. It details principle players, including AMCANOE-1 through AMCANOE-9, and reviews files related to efforts to unify exiles and support for Castro's overthrow, including an offer by the Cosa Nostra to assassinate Castro.

title: AMBRUSH Organization
summary: This memorandum discusses the AMBRUSH Organization, an Anti-Castro Security and Counter-Intelligence Team, and information regarding potential Cuban Communist penetration agents in the U.S. Government. It also includes information on various individuals and their alleged connections to Cuban intelligence and activities.

title: 1104-10308-10053 (2025 RELEASE UNDER THE PRESIDENT JOHN F. KENNEDY ASSASSINATION RECORDS ACT OF 1992)
recipient: DDP, ADDP, C/SOD, C/CI, C/FI, C/TSD, C/EE, C/SAS, S/CI
summary: This document discusses the potential implementation of sabotage operations against Cuban ships by AMLEGS (assets). It outlines possible consequences, including Cuban reprisals against Western carriers, increased security measures, and the reluctance of some AMLEGS to participate without assurance of a larger overthrow plan. Specific actions against the HAVANA ship are discussed, along with the potential use of explosives.

title: Classified Message Regarding Recruitment Activities in Cuba
summary: This document contains classified information related to recruitment activities, potential assets, and individuals of interest in Cuba. It references individuals identified as IDEN A, IDEN B, and IDEN C, and their connections to resistance groups and potential recruitment for ODYOKE. It also includes details on family members, residences, and visa applications.

title: Unsuccessful Exfiltration Attempt by M/V ADA, 9-12 May 1964
summary: Report on the unsuccessful exfiltration attempt by the M/V ADA from 9-12 May 1964, sponsored by AMLEO-3 to rescue his family. The operation involved recruiting individuals like Mario REMIS and Daniel (RODRIGUEZ) Santos, but was ultimately thwarted by Cuban authorities.

title: Report on Activities of AMWORLD
summary: This dispatch reports on the activities of AMWORLD in mid-July 1964, detailing information obtained from former members IDEN A and IDEN B. It covers topics such as commando instruction, intelligence operations, naval activities, operational briefings, AMBIDDY/1's activities, recreational houses, engineering, and a planned assassination mission.

title: AMFAUNA-26 Progress Report for October, November and December 1963
summary: This dispatch reports on the progress of AMFAUNA-26 operations from October to December 1963, including communication issues, attempts to activate radio systems, problems with deciphering materials, the arrest of AMFAUNA-38, and potential reasons for AMFAUNA-26's arrest. It also details reports made and expenses incurred during the period, and outlines future plans to maintain communication and exfiltrate endangered personnel.

title: Requirements Briefing to FBI Informant Going to Cuba
summary: This memo details the briefing of an FBI informant, Victor Thomas Vicente, before he travels to Cuba. It outlines his contacts, mission objectives related to gathering intelligence on Cuban-Soviet relations and internal security, and arrangements made by pro-Castro organizations.

title: RIOD 2944: GRYBAI TYPIC YORITE ANSTRUT
summary: This cable discusses a visit by Mario Rogerio Mestrinho de Mello to Cuba, rumors of an assassination attempt on Fidel Castro, travel restrictions, rumors about Lee Harvey Oswald in Mexico, and correspondence between Marianna Argüelles and A-1.

title: 2025 RELEASE UNDER THE PRESIDENT JOHN F. KENNEDY ASSASSINATION RECORDS ACT OF 1992
summary: This cable discusses several topics, including Juan Manuel Fernandez's desire to leave Cuba, a request to take Luis Rodriguez into the Jaguar Group, authorization to instruct A-35, information about an assassination attempt against Fidel Castro, the movement of tracked tanks, a Russian ship delivering fertilizer, and the defection of Commandant 'Contreras' and others.

title: RYBAT INDEVOUT 301
summary: Cable from MIDDAUGH to ZURC requesting assistance in obtaining books on espionage for a G-2 co-opted subject. Lists previously sent books and desired subjects.

title: Operational Exploitation of Khrushchev Visit to Cuba
summary: This document discusses plans to exploit Khrushchev's visit to Cuba by instigating a massive church manifestation or rally and spreading rumors of an assassination attempt. It details the involvement of various individuals and organizations, including Bishop Boza Masvidalis, Jose Lavastida, and CELAM, as well as media outlets like WRUL.

title: Identities of Individuals in Cuba
summary: This document contains information regarding the identities and roles of various individuals in Cuba, including military officers, police chiefs, and former revolutionaries. It mentions their involvement in significant events such as the Moncada attack, the Granma landing, and actions against Batista's regime. The document also notes individuals who are now unemployed or hiding, and provides details about their backgrounds and connections.

title: Agreement Between the United States Secret Service and the Central Intelligence Agency Concerning Presidential Protection in the United States
sender: Marshall S. Carter, Lieutenant General, USA, Deputy Director
recipient: Deputy Director for Plans, Deputy Director for Intelligence, Deputy Director for Science & Technology, Deputy Director for support
summary: This document contains an agreement between the United States Secret Service and the Central Intelligence Agency concerning presidential protection in the United States. It also includes memorandums for record discussing meetings, trips, and actions.

title: Chief, CI Meeting with Mr. Paul Wallach, Chief Counsel of Senate Select Committee on Intelligence
sender: Robert G. Wall, Deputy Chief, CI/OG
summary: Memorandum regarding a meeting between the Chief of CI and Mr. Paul Wallach, Chief Counsel of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, concerning access to Agency files related to the Lee Harvey Oswald case. The meeting addressed concerns about the Agency's cooperation and the sanitization of sensitive information. An agreement was reached for Senate Committee reviewers to work with the original files, with certain sensitive items sterilized or summarized, subject to spot checks. The agreement was approved by Mr. Blee.

title: Supplementary Information on James Earl Ray
sender: David H. Blee, Associate Deputy Director for Operations
summary: This document contains supplementary information on James Earl Ray, including discussions with the FBI and a cable regarding Eric Galt, a suspect in the assassination of Martin Luther King, Jr. It details efforts to determine Galt's whereabouts and requests information from various locations.

title: RECORDS REVIEW BOARD AND DEPT OF STATE REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE IN APPROACHING FSB/SVR FOR OSWALD FILE
summary: This cable discusses the Assassinations Records Review Board's (ARRB) request for assistance in approaching the FSB/SVR for the Lee Harvey Oswald file. The ARRB is seeking access to the KGB records on Oswald, which were originally held in Minsk but flown to Moscow in 1963 following the assassination, then returned to Minsk. The cable seeks station thoughts on the proposal to approach the FSB/SVR seeking access to the file and discusses implications of such a request.

title: BKGB Access Support to USG Assassination Record Review Board
summary: This cable discusses the USG's Assassination Records Review Board (ARRB) interest in obtaining BKGB (Belarusian KGB) records related to Lee Harvey Oswald's time in Minsk. It details previous inquiries, obstacles faced due to Belarusian privacy laws, and potential future requests for assistance. It also mentions Norman Mailer's access to these records and the BKGB's subsequent dissatisfaction.

title: NEW STORY ON LEE HARVEY OSWALD AND CIA IN JAPAN
summary: This cable discusses a new story on Lee Harvey Oswald and the CIA in Japan. It suggests the COS have the embassy press officer refer the UPI correspondent to the Public Affairs Staff (PAS). PAS recommends treating the UPI correspondent like any other reporter and suggests directing questions to PAS.

title: NEWS STORY ON LEE HARVEY OSWALD AND CIA IN JAPAN
summary: This cable discusses a news story about Lee Harvey Oswald and the CIA in Japan. It requests the name and phone number of the project office responsible for declassification of Kennedy assassination papers, as a UPI reporter is about to file a story based on local research and an interview with a retired Marine officer who claimed Oswald was recruited by the CIA while stationed in Japan in the 1950s.

title: RELEASE OF CLASSIFIED DOCUMENT
summary: This cable discusses the release of a classified document related to Lee Harvey Oswald. It notes that the received fax appears incomplete and requests that crypts be deleted before release. The station also wants to be informed of the release date to notify the ambassador and liaison service chiefs.

title: WASHINGTON POST ARTICLE ON MEXICO CITY TELTAPS
summary: A Washington Post article discusses CIA activities in Mexico City during the JFK assassination timeframe, specifically mentioning a wiretap operation carried out with the cooperation of the Mexican government. The CIA had attempted to block the release of these documents, declassified under the JFK Assassination Records Collection Act of 1992, fearing it might endanger similar ongoing operations. The station is asked to comment on any reaction by liaison (particularly KDSOMBRERO) or unilateral assets to this disclosure.

title: BRIEFING PAPER AND OSWALD FILES
summary: This cable discusses a briefing paper for CODEL Shelby regarding Oswald files, a historical conversation with a local service about those files, and a diplomatic note submitted by the Ambassador requesting the files on Oswald.

title: DRAFT BRIEFING PAPER AND OSWALD FILES
summary: This cable discusses a draft briefing paper and the Lee Harvey Oswald files. It includes instructions to correct the briefing paper to reflect changes requested, information about the offer to provide the Oswald files being turned over to the FBI due to the sensitivity connected with the Kennedy assassination, and requests to delete or soften certain sections of the briefing paper related to unilateral operations, embassy security, and personnel requirements.

title: REQUEST FOR GUIDANCE
classification: John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Act
summary: This cable discusses a request for guidance regarding files on Lee Harvey Oswald and the transfer of information to the FBI. It also mentions discussions with a source (JYVAPOROUS) regarding access to the Oswald files in Minsk and the FBI's potential involvement.

title: REQUEST FOR GUIDANCE
summary: This cable discusses a request for guidance regarding potential questioning of JYVAPOROUS about sharing files on Lee Harvey Oswald with the USG and Norman Mailer.

title: JFK ASSASSINATION ISSUES
summary: This cable discusses the potential impact of disclosing information related to Oswald's tapes and the use of NOCs (Non-Official Covers) on the liaison relationship with Mexican authorities, particularly concerning joint TELTAP operations and the sensitivity surrounding the NWBOLTON relationship.

title: 11 NOVEMBER 1993 Meeting with the SVRR
summary: Cable discusses a meeting between the COS and Leonid Ryabchenya of the SVRR regarding various topics, including a book by Oleg Nechiporenko on Lee Harvey Oswald, scheduling of discussions on Yugoslavia, and an unclassified paper from U.S. scientists on environmental issues.

title: WASHINGTON TIMES ARTICLE RE KGB OFFER TO HOLLYWOOD
summary: This cable discusses a Washington Times article regarding a KGB offer to Hollywood and its possible connection to the LWOPUS case. It explores similarities between the KGB's approach and LWOPUS's offer of a manuscript, including financial motivations, volume of material, potential joint efforts, and concerns for safety.

title: House Select Committee on Assassinations Request for Access to the "Hart Report" and related documents on Yuri Nosenko
summary: This document includes multiple memos and attachments regarding Yuri Nosenko, a KGB defector, and his connections to Lee Harvey Oswald and the Kennedy assassination. It covers topics such as the release of information related to Nosenko, requests for access to documents, and internal discussions regarding the handling of Nosenko's case.

title: Position on Release of Information Pertaining to Mexico City Station and the JFK Assassination Records
sender: Fredrick C. Wickham, Jr./David N. Edger/Linda C. Cipriani/J. Barry Harrelson/David Cohen
recipient: Chief, Historical Review Group/Director, Intelligence Coordination, Intelligence and Research, Department of State/J. Barry Harrelson/Fredrick Wickham/Johnny Goins/Eleanor E. Neiman
summary: Collection of documents regarding CIA's position on releasing information pertaining to Mexico City Station and the JFK Assassination Records. Also includes notes from meetings with ARRB staff and correspondence regarding the release of various CIA stations.

title: JFK Assassination Records Collection Act of 1992 Compliance Documents
summary: This document contains correspondence, declarations, and memoranda related to the CIA's compliance with the JFK Assassination Records Collection Act of 1992. It includes letters from George Tenet, Director of Central Intelligence, to John R. Tunheim, Chair of the Assassination Records Review Board, declarations from Edmund Cohen and David W. Carey regarding the CIA's search and release of assassination-related records, and internal memoranda concerning the handling and replacement of declaration pages.

title: Agency Records on the JFK Assassination
summary: This document primarily consists of correspondence between the CIA and the House Committee on Government Operations regarding CIA holdings of records related to the assassination of President Kennedy. It also includes outlines of testimony and internal memos regarding the JFK resolution and related hearings.

title: JFK Records Review - Lessons Learned
summary: This memo discusses lessons learned from the CIA's JFK Records Review project, including challenges posed by unrealistic deadlines, inflexible standards, and mandated procedures. It also covers the review process, the JFK Act, and ARRB requests for information.

title: Cuban Subversion in Latin America Since July 1963
origin_agency: Central Intelligence Agency, Office of Current Intelligence
summary: This Current Intelligence Memorandum discusses Cuban subversion in Latin America since July 1963. This document discusses the status of relations between the FBI and CIA, instances of cooperation between the two agencies, and possible topics that CIA Director McCone may refer to, including security concerns, coverage of diplomatic establishments, and defectors.

title: CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY INFORMATION RECEIVED FROM JAMES ANGLETON
summary: This document discusses James Angleton, a CIA official in charge of the Special Projects unit, and recommends creating a control file for the information he provides to the FBI. It also alerts Section Chiefs regarding the handling of information received from Angleton.

title: JAMES ANGLETON CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY
summary: This document discusses James Angleton's request for a uniform procedure in transmitting mail to him, ensuring his identity is not revealed to other agencies due to his involvement in sensitive projects like Israeli Intelligence. It also mentions that correspondence dealing with Israeli Intelligence matters should be directed to James Angleton.

title: JAMES ANGLETON
summary: This document discusses James Angleton of the CIA providing information to the FBI on a confidential basis and the procedure for handling this information to protect Angleton and the CIA as sources.

title: BUREAU INFORMANT 200
summary: Memorandum regarding Bureau Informant 200, a procedure approved in 1954 to attribute information received from James Angleton, CIA, sourced from the Israeli Intelligence Service and other sources under Angleton's control. The information concerns the travel of U.S. citizens to Russia via Israel.

title: CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY (CIA) INFORMATION RECEIVED FROM JAMES ANGLETON
summary: This document discusses the creation of a control file (62-99724) under the caption, "CIA - James Angleton," for retaining copies of certain memoranda disseminated by James Angleton, Chief Counterintelligence Staff, CIA. It recommends discontinuing the practice of placing copies of Bureau Informant 100 material in the control file, while retaining the file for policy-related mail.

title: ANTI CASTRO ACTIVITIES IS-CUBA
summary: This document discusses anti-Castro activities and mentions conversations with CIA contacts regarding potential actions against Cuba and opinions on US policy towards the country.

title: ANTI-FIDEL CASTRO ACTIVITIES
summary: This document discusses anti-Castro activities and a meeting between Robert Kleberg and Vice-President Lyndon B. Johnson regarding US plans for Cuba.

title: SANTIAGO ALVAREZ RODRIGUEZ
summary: This FBI report from August 4, 1961, discusses the closure of the investigation into Santiago Alvarez Rodriguez due to his relative inactivity in Cuban revolutionary matters. The report mentions CIA's past operational interest in Alvarez during the Bay of Pigs invasion and their current interest in his son, Santiago Alvarez. It also references a CIA communication about Alvarez's involvement with the publication 'Esbirros,' a scandal sheet against various Cuban groups.

title: Report on SANTIAGO ALVAREZ RODRIGUEZ
summary: Report regarding SANTIAGO ALVAREZ RODRIGUEZ and potential anti-Castro activities, including information from informants and planned interviews with individuals connected to BATISTA.
FBI administrative folder regarding the HSCA and Lee Harvey Oswald, including memos, A/Ts, TTYs, letters, notes, LHM, press releases, testimony, news articles, and translations.

title: MARTIN GREENDLINGER, aka SECURITY MATTER - C
summary: Memo from LEGAT, BONN to DIRECTOR, FBI regarding MARTIN GREENDLINGER and inquiries made to various agencies about his travels and activities.

title: Untitled
summary: This document contains information about counter-revolutionary activities in Cuba, including planned raids, arms drops, and contacts between individuals in Cuba and Miami.

title: LUCIEN CONEIN
summary: This document is a memo from the FBI regarding Lucien Conein. It discusses his affiliation with the CIA and his current assignment in Saigon, South Vietnam. It also details a request from the CIA that no information be furnished to the French regarding Conein's affiliation or whereabouts.

title: Report on Robert Glenn Thompson and William K. Harvey
summary: This document is a report from the FBI regarding Robert Glenn Thompson, also known as Robert F. Laudwein, and William K. Harvey. It references previous reports and clarifies information related to Thompson's story in the 'Saturday Evening Post.' The document also mentions the code name 'OXTANK' and includes administrative details and dissemination records.

title: Interview with ROBERT GLENN THOMPSON regarding CIA and Army Intelligence Personnel in Berlin
summary: This document contains an interview with ROBERT GLENN THOMPSON regarding his knowledge of individuals associated with the CIA and Army Intelligence in Berlin, including WILLIAM K. HARVEY and CLARK JUNG. THOMPSON was interviewed about his time with OSI, Berlin, and his interactions with a Soviet principal named STEVEN.

title: CIA EFFORTS TO PENETRATE USSR
summary: This document contains interview transcripts and information regarding CIA efforts to penetrate the USSR, as well as interviews with various CIA personnel, including William K. Harvey, Serge Peter Karlow, and others. It also includes details about specific operations, personnel assignments, and travel in Europe during the 1950s.

title: FRANC PECAR and JOSEPH RAYMOND MEROLA
summary: FBI memo to CIA regarding FRANC PECAR and JOSEPH RAYMOND MEROLA, discussing CIA's interest in contacting PECAR to persuade him to return to Yugoslavia under CIA control. FBI does not recommend approaching PECAR.

title: Memorandum Regarding Franc Pecar
recipient: HQ, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Attention: Mr. S. J. Papich
summary: This memo discusses Franc Pecar, a Yugoslav trade official, who may wish to remain in the U.S. The CIA is interested in potentially persuading him to return to Yugoslavia.

This memo from the CIA to the FBI discusses Franc Pecar, who arrived in Miami on April 4, 1963. The CIA is considering contacting Pecar during his visit to Vienna for recruitment purposes and requests information from the FBI regarding Pecar's activities in the United States.

title: CLIP
summary: This document discusses Joseph Raymond Merola's alleged connections to the CIA and his potential involvement in supplying weapons to anti-Castro groups and hoodlum acquaintances.

title: CR 97-3224-NR
summary: This document discusses investigations by the CIA and U.S. Army Attache in Managua, Nicaragua, and Guatemala City, Guatemala, regarding Manuel Fuego, Mitchell Livingston Werbell, and associated activities. It mentions contacts with Noel Pallais, General Anastasio Somoza, Lucy Luchien, and Arthur L. Smith. The document also details surveillance and telephone conversations monitored by the Judicial Police in Guatemala.

title: [Restricted]
summary: This document discusses ANTONIO HECTOR RIVERO JUARRERO, who is associated with MITCHELL LIVINGSTON WERBELL and suspected of gambling enterprises.

title: FRANCISCO RODRIGUEZ TAMAYO
summary: This FBI report discusses Francisco Rodriguez Tamayo and the Pan America Confederation, referencing informants and telephone numbers in Key West, Florida.

title: Eloy Gutierrez Menoyo
summary: This document is a correlation summary regarding Eloy Gutierrez Menoyo, including information about his activities, associations, and reputation among Cuban exiles and intelligence agencies. It contains reports from informants, CIA information, and references to other documents related to Menoyo and his involvement with various anti-Castro groups and activities.

title: PETROS MOUTSOS
summary: This memo discusses Petros Moutsos, a former CIA informant in the Greek Maritime Organization (OENO), who is now being considered for a mission in Cuba. The CIA plans to have him jump ship in New Orleans and travel to Cuba, where he will gather information. They also hope he can re-establish contact with his wife, Angela Boyer, to gain access to communist circles in Cuba.

title: CIA LIAISON MATERIAL
summary: This memo concerns Petros Moutsos, a former CIA informant in the communist-dominated Greek Maritime Organization (OENO). CIA is planning to have Moutsos travel to Cuba as a source of information and wants him to jump ship in New Orleans with INS approval. He will also attempt to contact his wife, Angela Boyer, who has a communist background, to improve his contacts in communist circles in Cuba.

title: LEVI LAUB UNAUTHORIZED TRAVEL TO CUBA
summary: FBI memo regarding Levi Laub's unauthorized travel to Cuba, based on information from the CIA and British Intelligence Service (MI-6).

title: [Restricted]
summary: FBI memo to CIA regarding EDUARDO ESPINOSA Y PRIETO and his possible connections to communist activities. The FBI clarifies information about bank drafts he wrote and advises against suggesting he financed Communist Party activities in a summary to the Bundesunt fuer Verfassungsschutz (BFV), Germany.

title: [Restricted]
summary: This document pertains to Henryk Ignacy Janikowski and includes information from a West German service regarding a check from Eduardo Espinosa y Prieto of the Mexican Embassy in Moscow to Erik Schott, an architect in Bremen, Germany. It also details Janikowski's activities involving buying and shipping used cars, obtaining dollars from the black market, and potential customs duty evasion.

title: CIA LIAISON MATERIAL JORGE BELIARD
summary: This memo discusses Jorge Beliard, a station manager for Cubana Airlines, and a CIA request regarding his potential use in establishing courier routes between Cuba and the United States. The FBI is considering whether to allow CIA contact with Beliard or to handle the contact themselves.

title: NY 3186-PS
summary: This document discusses the CIA's desire to contact a person of security interest (PSI) who is a station manager for Cubana Airlines in New York City, in connection with Cuban operations, specifically to establish courier routes between the U.S. and Cuba. The FBI is considering whether to allow the CIA to contact the PSI, operate independently, or act as an intermediary.

title: [Restricted]
summary: This document discusses Eduardo Espinosa y Prieto, a Mexican Ambassador, and his potential ties to Soviet intelligence. It includes information from the FBI and requests permission to share information with German authorities.

title: CIA LIAISON MATERIAL
summary: FBI memo regarding CIA liaison material and Enrique Garcia Armenteros. CIA has placed a man in Cuba to develop information related to a Bureau lead.

title: CIA LIAISON MATERIAL
summary: FBI requests CIA assistance in obtaining papers from Garcia in Cuba, potentially containing intelligence or propaganda data. The State Department prefers CIA to handle the matter.

title: PAUL HICKMAN INFORMATION CONCERNING Communist Party-Cuba
summary: FBI memo regarding Paul Hickman's alleged involvement in arms sales to the Castro government and his contact with a Soviet Embassy representative.

title: SOVIET EMBASSY HAVANA, CUBA
summary: This document discusses the shipment of ten safes from the Mosler Safe Company to the Soviet Embassy in Havana, Cuba. It includes details about the safe models, serial numbers, combinations, and dial key numbers. The CIA is provided with a set of dial keys and keys for the inside compartments of the safes.

title: MANUEL PINEIRO
summary: Memorandum regarding Manuel Pineiro, a high-ranking official in the Cuban G-2 organization, and CIA's tentative conclusion that Pineiro is identical with Petronio, who has been mentioned in messages made available to the Bureau and CIA.

title: CIA LIAISON MATERIAL
summary: This memo discusses Ismael Rodriguez, the comptroller of Cubana Airlines, who was used as a source of information by the Bureau and as a courier for transmitting material between the US and Cuba for CIA operations.

title: HERBERT LEVY
summary: FBI memo to CIA regarding Herbert Levy and his previous interactions with a CIA representative concerning information about India. Levy provided information on Cuban economic matters and possible violations of export regulations.

title: LARGE QUANTITIES OF JUTE BAGS AND HESSIAN CLOTH SOUGHT BY CUBAN GOVERNMENT BY PURCHASE OR BARTER THROUGH INTERNATIONAL ORE AND FERTILIZER COMPANY, NEW YORK CITY
summary: FBI memo regarding Cuban government seeking jute bags and hessian cloth through International Ore and Fertilizer Company, and CIA's past connection with Herbert Levy of St. Regis Paper Company for economic information gathering in India.

title: FOREIGN POLITICAL MATTERS - CUBA
classification: Foreign Political Matters, Cuba, CIA Liaison Material
summary: This document contains a memo from the FBI regarding Raul Roa, Cuban Foreign Minister, commenting on the Sino-Indian conflict and the situation in Cuba in 1963. Roa's evaluation of the situation in Cuba was highly pessimistic and he expressed concerns about the United Nations and the Organization of American States (OAS).

title: ANGELA PRINCE MOUTSOS
summary: FBI memo to CIA concerning Angela Prince Moutsos and her possible residence and activities in Cuba. Moutsos' husband, Pedros Moutsos, was a former CIA informant.

title: ANGELA PRINCE MOUTSOS aka
summary: FBI memo regarding Angela Prince Moutsos and her activities in Cuba, including her husband's connection to the CIA.

title: PERMANENT STUDENT COMMITTEE FOR TRAVEL TO CUBA IS-C
summary: FBI memo regarding the Permanent Student Committee for Travel to Cuba and information provided by Mark Tischman to a CIA source in Madrid about fellow travelers and their ideologies.

title: YURI IVANOVICH NOSENKO ESP - R (KGB)
summary: This document contains information from an interview with Yuri Ivanovich Nosenko on April 2, 1964, where he provides details on various cases and individuals of interest to the FBI, including potential KGB contacts, American tourists, and defectors.

title: CIA REORGANIZATION
summary: Arthur Schlesinger Jr. wrote to President Kennedy on June 10, 1961, regarding CIA reorganization, covert action, paramilitary warfare, Cuba, and policy control. He suggests that CIA operations have not been effectively subordinate to U.S. foreign policy. He also suggests that State can be informed of such operations at an early enough stage to affect the conception and preliminary planning of the operation.

title: Testimony of William Harvey
summary: This document is a transcript of the testimony of William Harvey on June 25, 1975. The testimony covers subjects such as ZRRIFLE, Castro, Johnny Roselli, Operation Mongoose, Richard Bissell, assassinations, John F. Kennedy, QJWIN, the Mafia, and Arnold Silver.

title: TESTIMONY OF WILLIAM K. HARVEY
summary: Testimony of William K. Harvey concerning Operation Mongoose, Johnny Rosselli, Castro assassination attempts, poison pills, Cuba, John McCone, CIA, Richard Bissell, White House, Mafia, Dan Rowan, and Sam Giancana.

title: TESTIMONY OF DAVID ATLEE PHILLIPS
summary: This document is a transcript of the testimony of David Atlee Phillips before the SSCIA on July 31, 1975. The testimony covers a range of topics including the CIA, Cuba, Castro, Lansky, Meyer, Bay of Pigs, Assassination, Trafficante, Santos, Ruby, Jack, Chile, Allende, and Operation Mongoose.

title: ALLEGED CUBAN PLAN TO ASSASSINATE PRESIDENT OF PANAMA
recipient: State Department; Central Intelligence Agency; Department of the Army; Department of the Air Force; Department of the Navy
summary: FBI report regarding an alleged Cuban plan to assassinate the President of Panama in order to create additional uprisings in that country. The information was provided by Orlando Piedra, formerly connected with Federal Police in Cuba.

title: MEETING WITH THE WARREN COMMISSION ON 12 MARCH 1964
summary: This document details a meeting between the CIA and the Warren Commission on March 12, 1964, discussing the investigation of Lee Harvey Oswald's activities in Mexico City, CIA's file on Oswald, information sharing with other agencies, and potential leads related to Jack Ruby.

title: Robert Maheu
summary: This document discusses Robert Maheu's involvement in arranging a party for a foreign Head of State in 1959, involving a prominent actress. The Office of Security requested special support during the Los Angeles and New York phases of the tour, with arrangements made through Gregson Bautzer. The actress met with the foreign official in both Los Angeles and New York.

title: ROBERT MAHEU'S TRANSPORTATION OF PROSTITUTES
summary: This document discusses Robert Maheu's alleged transportation of prostitutes for a foreign leader and wiretapping activities. It also mentions potential blackmail attempts against the U.S. government.

title: Testimony Regarding CIA Background and Alleged Assassination Plots
summary: This document is a part of testimony where Mr. Harvey discusses his background in the CIA, including his roles in the Soviet Intelligence Branch and his assignments in Berlin and Rome. He denies any personal knowledge of assassination plans or plots within the Agency concerning Patrice Lumumba or any other foreign leader apart from Fidel Castro.

title: TESTIMONY OF ROBERT MAHEU
summary: Testimony of Robert Maheu regarding various CIA operations, including wiretaps, attempts to influence foreign leaders, and film production.

title: DESPOSITION/TRANSCRIPT OF STURBITTS, WILLIAM C.
summary: This is a deposition/transcript of William C. Sturbitts. He discusses Cuban operations, Miami Station, and Task Force W. He also discusses possible assassination attempts against Fidel Castro.

title: Miscellaneous Records of the Church Committee
summary: This document contains information pertaining to William Harvey, ZRRIFLE, and Operation Mongoose. It includes meeting agendas, chronologies, and memorandums related to intelligence activities and potential assassination plots involving Fidel Castro.
This document contains information on anti-Castro activities, organized crime, the CIA, and the assassination of John F. Kennedy.

title: Memorandum for the Record: Minutes of Special Group Meeting, 6 June 1961
summary: Minutes of Special Group Meeting on June 6, 1961, covering topics such as the Congo, political action projects, Francis Gary Powers' release procedures, STPOLLY flight in Vietnam, covert annexes for Vietnam and Korea, TACKLE, Nicaragua, and the Agency's relations with exile groups in Cuba.

title: Memo to President CIA Reorganization
summary: Arthur Schlesinger Jr. sends a memo to President Kennedy regarding CIA reorganization, emphasizing the need for greater oversight and control due to concerns about autonomy and potential for errors. The memo suggests reforms in clandestine operations, policy integration, and intelligence management.

title: CIA Reorganization
summary: Arthur Schlesinger Jr. submits a memorandum to President Kennedy regarding the reorganization of the CIA, its autonomy, clandestine operations, relationship with foreign policy, and intelligence gathering.

title: Withdrawal of United Nations Troops from the Congo
summary: This document discusses plans for the withdrawal of United Nations troops from the Congo at the end of 1963, despite Congolese Premier Cyrille Adoula's requests to the contrary. A new method of financing the Congo operation, maintaining 40-50 percent troop strength, is suggested, but the Secretary General's ability to accept outside funds is debated.

title: Fidel Castro's Coming Visit to Moscow and Algiers
summary: Report on Fidel Castro's planned visit to Moscow and Algiers in April 1963, including the purpose of the visits and the relationships between Castro, Khrushchev, Ben Bella, and Boumedienne.

title: Central Intelligence Agency Information Report: Possible Establishment of a Cuban Exile Base in Nicaragua
summary: This document discusses the possible establishment of a Cuban exile base in Nicaragua in 1963, potential support from the U.S., and the policies of various Cuban exile groups.

title: Central Intelligence Agency Information Report
summary: This document contains information about Cuban exile plans to attack the Cuban mainland and launch Plan Omega, which involves reorganizing guerrilla groups, attacking Russian bases and Cuban forces, and coordinating a general insurrection. It also mentions the alliance receiving blueprints of major plants inside Cuba and the involvement of the Frente Anti-Comunista de Liberacion (FAL) within the Cuban Army.

title: Activities of Cuban Trained Peruvian Guerrillas
summary: This memorandum details the activities of Cuban-trained Peruvian guerrillas, focusing on their training in Cuba, clandestine return to Peru, and plans for a revolution. It highlights the involvement of the Movimiento Izquierda Revolucionario (MIR) and the coordination efforts in Paris, as well as the financial support from Chinese Communists.

title: Draft Briefing Notes: Funding
summary: This document contains draft briefing notes from February 18, 1963, regarding Cuban financing of subversive operations in Latin America. It details instances of cash transfers, bank transfers, and bank robberies linked to Cuban support for guerrilla and political activities in Venezuela, Nicaragua, Ecuador, Guatemala, Brazil, Peru, and Argentina.

title: Meeting of Vietnam Task Force June 19 1961
summary: This document is a memorandum from Johnson to Rostow regarding a meeting of the Task Force on Vietnam on June 19, 1961. The meeting covered intelligence briefings, local currency costs, the situation in Laos, and other matters. Cottrell's proposal to break off the Geneva Conference and intervene in Laos was discussed, as well as a possible 100,000 man increase in GVN forces.

title: Opposition in Khanh Hoa Province
summary: This document discusses opposition in Khanh Hoa Province to arming mountain tribesmen and the Strategic Hamlet Program, as well as conflict among provincial authorities.

title: Possible severence of Cambodian
recipient: STATE ARMY NAVY AIR USMACV MAAG USOM CINCPAC PACFLT ARPAC PACAF 9TH FIELD STATION
summary: This document discusses the possible severance of Cambodian-South Vietnamese diplomatic relations.

title: Vietnamese Communist Analysis of Effects
recipient: STATE, ARMY, NAVY, AIR, JCS, SECDEF, NSA, NIC, USIA, OCI, ONE, OCR, ORR, AID, DIA
summary: This document is a Vietnamese Communist analysis of the effects of increased U.S. military aid to the Government of Vietnam, written in early May 1962 by a VC company commander in Ba Xuyen Province.

title: Views... Possible Coup D'Etat
recipient: STATE, ARMY/ACSI, NAVY, AIR, JCS, SECDEF, NSA, NIC, USIA, OCI, ONE, OCR, LORR
summary: This document discusses the views of Colonel Ton That Xung regarding the possibility of a coup d'etat in South Vietnam. He indicates that plans for such action would not be communicated to the Americans due to the US opposition to unlawful acts.

title: Vietnam Communist Activities
recipient: STATE, ARMY/ACSI, NAVY, AIR, JCS, SECDEF, NSA, NIC, USIA, OCI, ONE, OCR, ORR, OO, DIA, EX, AID, USMACV, MAAG, USOM, CINCPAC, PACFLT, ARPAC, PACAF
summary: This document discusses Vietnamese Communist activities in the Saigon area, including the infiltration of VC into Saigon, the deployment of an armed platoon for special operations, and plans to set up a base among laborers for future operations. It also mentions potential sabotage and kidnappings, and an unconfirmed report about a possible large-scale attack.

title: Indication of Planning
recipient: STATE INR DIA ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR JCS SECDEF NSA. NIC AID US IA OCI STATE/DIR
summary: This document indicates planning for the reoccupation of North Vietnam in late October 1962. It involves drafting questionnaires for people in South Vietnam and those formerly living in North Vietnam to gather information on acquaintances still in North Vietnam.

title: Ngo Dinh Nhu's Statement on Withdrawal of American Aid
summary: This telegram reports on Ngo Dinh Nhu's statements regarding the potential withdrawal of American aid from South Vietnam. Nhu discussed revising policies on receiving aid and prioritizing different categories of aid, emphasizing self-sufficiency. The telegram also mentions instructions to encourage local weapons production and concerns among Vietnamese Air Force officers about the potential collapse of the regime without American support.

title: Central Intelligence Agency Information Report
recipient: STATE/INR DIA ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR STATE/DIR JCS SECDEF NSA NIC
summary: This document discusses the tensions between the Government of Vietnam and the U.S. Government over operations in South Vietnam in mid-April 1963. Diem and Nhu were concerned over "infringements" of Vietnamese sovereignty, particularly by the U.S. Special Forces. Diem plans to confront Ambassador Nolting and USMACV Chief General Harkins with evidence and demand a reduction in the number of U.S. personnel in South Vietnam.

title: Central Intelligence Agency Information Report
recipient: STATE/INR DIA ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR JCS SECDEF NSA. NIC A.ID USIA OC I ONE OCR ORR OBI 00 IDII
summary: This document contains information regarding Viet Cong concentration on terrorist and military subversion activity in the capital area of South Vietnam in early April 1963. It details plans to increase terrorist activity, target Americans, and reorganize counterpropaganda personnel.

title: Central Intelligence Agency Information Report: Plans for a Coup D'Etat in Central Vietnam by the Reformed VNQDD
summary: This document contains an intelligence report about plans for a coup d'etat in Central Vietnam by the reformed VNQDD. The report details the organization's structure, planned actions, and potential consequences, including the possible exploitation by the Viet Cong.

title: Central Intelligence Agency Information Report: Apprehensions of Vietnamese Consul General in Singapore Regarding Recent Events in Vietnam
summary: Vietnamese Consul General in Singapore expresses concerns about recent political acts in Vietnam that may weaken the Diem regime, including the dismissal of officials and the Hue incident involving Buddhist protesters.

title: CIA Information Telegram
recipient: STATE/INR DIA ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR JCS SECDEF NSA NIC AID USIA OCI ONE OCR STATE/DIR ORR OB 00 EXO
summary: This document is a CIA Information Telegram discussing discussions between President Diem of South Vietnam and Vice President Chen Cheng of Nationalist China in March 1963. The discussions covered topics such as increased Chinese Nationalist military support for South Vietnam, the use of South Vietnam as a base for Chinese Nationalist military operations against mainland China, and joint operations into North Vietnam and Laos.

title: CIA Information Telegram
summary: CIA information telegram regarding the seeking of American support for the overthrow of the Diem regime in South Vietnam.

title: CIA Information Report
recipient: STATE/INR DIA ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR JCS SECDEF NIC NSA AID USIA OCI ONE OCR ORR 081 00 STATE/DIR
summary: This document is a CIA information report regarding a white paper being prepared by Gene Gregory of the Times of Vietnam at the request of Madame Ngo Dinh Nhu. The white paper sets forth the Government of Vietnam's position on the Buddhist issue, American presence and policy in South Vietnam.

title: CIA Information Telegram: Coup D'Etat Plan of Ngo Dinh Nhu
summary: This document discusses a potential coup d'etat being planned by Ngo Dinh Nhu against the Diem government in South Vietnam in July 1963. Nhu is reportedly seeking support from army generals and believes a swift, overnight coup is necessary. The document also mentions concerns about the influence of Buddhist leaders and the need for immediate action given the upcoming arrival of a new US ambassador.

title: CIA Information Telegram
recipient: STATE, USMACY, CINCPAC, PACFLT, ARPACO, PACAF, CORS
summary: This document discusses the status of a coup d'etat plan by Tran Kim Tuyen's group against President Diem in South Vietnam, including details of the plan and the timing of the coup.

title: CIA Information Telegram
recipient: STATE INR DIA ARMY ACSI NAVYAIR JCS SECDEF NSA NIC STATE/DIR GROUP AID USIA OCI ONE OCR ORR
summary: This document discusses a possible change in the Government of Vietnam's foreign policy due to the appointment of Ambassador Lodge. It also mentions President Diem's concerns about the appointment and the recall of diplomats for consultation.

title: CIA Information Telegram
recipient: State/INR DIA ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR JCS SECDEF. NSA NIG AID YSIA OGI. ONE OGR STATE D'I'R CIB
summary: This document is a CIA Information Telegram, discussing Major General Duong Van Minh's comments on the current situation in South Vietnam and the need for a change in the government. It details Minh's criticism of President Diem, the Buddhist issue, and potential scenarios involving other key figures.

title: CIA Information Telegram
recipient: STATE (AMBASSADOR LODGE), USMACV (GENERAL HARKINS), CINCPAC ARPAC PACAF PACFLT
summary: CIA Information Telegram regarding General Nguyen Khanh's plans to make a final decision on action against the Diem regime in South Vietnam, dated September 19, 1963.

title: CIA Information Telegram
summary: CIA Information Telegram regarding Pham Ngoc Thao and the Tuyen Group's plan to launch a coup d'etat in South Vietnam.

title: CIA Information Telegram
summary: CIA Information Telegram regarding the planned suicide of Ambassador Buu Hoi's mother, Dieu Hue, in protest of Buddhist persecution in Vietnam.

title: CIA Information Report
recipient: JCS, SECDEF, NSA, NIC, CCI, STATE, INF, DIA, ARMY, ACSI, NAVY, AIR
summary: This document is a CIA information report from October 8, 1963, providing a situation appraisal of South Vietnam as of October 5, 1963. It discusses coup plotting, demands by generals to President Diem, the atmosphere in Saigon, and potential surprises for the upcoming National Day celebrations. It also touches on the Viet Cong's lack of capitalizing on opportunities and potential GVN-DRV rapprochement.

title: Plans of Government to assassinate Ambassador Lodge, other high embassy officials, and Thich Tri Quang, and burn the Chancery
summary: CIA report regarding plans of the Government of Vietnam to assassinate Ambassador Lodge and other high embassy officials, as well as Thich Tri Quang, and to burn the Chancery.

title: CIA Information Report
recipient: STATE/INR DIA ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR JCS SECDEF NSA NIC AID USIA OCI STATE/DIR
summary: CIA Information Report regarding a recommendation by cabinet officers that Nhu be made Prime Minister in South Vietnam.

title: CIA Information Report: HUYNH VAN LANG COUP MOVE TIMING
recipient: STATE (AMBASSADOR LODGE) USMACV (GENERAL HARKINS) CINCPAC PACAF ARPAC PACFLT
summary: This document is a CIA information report detailing a planned coup in South Vietnam against President Diem, scheduled for late September or early October 1963. It identifies key figures involved, including Generals Tran Thien Khiem, Nguyen Khanh, and Duong Van Minh, and outlines the planned military actions and forces to be used. The report also mentions the challenges in executing the coup, such as breaching Diem's bunker, and the concerns about potential U.S. involvement or disapproval.

title: CIA Information Report
summary: This document is a CIA information report about Ngo Dinh Nhu's intention to deal with the Viet Cong and attempts of Pham Ngoc Thao to arrange VNAF support for a coup d'etat.

title: CIA Information Report
summary: This document contains information about the planning of a coup in South Vietnam in September 1963. It details the involvement of various military figures and their concerns about the political situation and Viet Cong activity. It also discusses the potential for United States support and the reorganization of the government following the coup.

title: Cable from Bundy to Lodge Regarding Potential Coup in Vietnam
summary: This document is a cable from McGeorge Bundy at the White House to Ambassador Lodge in Saigon, dated October 30, 1963. It discusses the U.S. position on a potential coup in South Vietnam, particularly the extent to which the U.S. should influence or intervene in such an event.

title: Status Report on Southeast Asia
sender: Task Force Southeast Asia, Department of State
summary: This document is a status report on Southeast Asia, dated July 11, 1962, prepared by the Task Force Southeast Asia, Department of State. It covers the current situation in Viet-Nam, Thailand, Laos, Burma, and Cambodia, focusing on military, political, and economic developments.

title: CIA Information Telegram: Comments of Yugoslav and Bloc Diplomats on the Probable Effect of Kennedy Assassination on East-West Relations
summary: This telegram discusses the reactions of Yugoslavian and Soviet Bloc diplomats to President Kennedy's assassination and the potential impact on East-West relations. Diplomats express concerns about the future of US-Soviet relations, the strength of right-wing elements in the US, and the potential slowing of improved relations.

title: Information Report Re: Offer of Supplies and Men to the Governor of Rio Grande do Sul by the Governments of Communist China and Cuba
recipient: STATE, ARMY/ACSI NAVY AIR JCS SECDEF NSA NIC USIA OCI ONE OCR ORR OO EXO FBI I&NS TREASURY
summary: This document reports on an offer of supplies and men to the Governor of Rio Grande do Sul by the governments of Communist China and Cuba.

title: Information Report Re: Views

summary: This document is an information report telegram from the CIA regarding the views of the British Ambassador to South Vietnam, H.A.F. Hohler, on a neutralist solution for South Vietnam.
